abstract: Retinal resistivity is a key parameter for modeling both the electric field in tissue and the resulting neural response - a crucial step in designing retinal prostheses, especially since both depend on resistivity nonlinearly. Previous studies using penetrating microelectrodes reported vastly different values, varying by as much as two orders of magnitude, likely due to parasitic capacitance in microelectrodes, compression of tissue and its rupture by the inserted probe, allowing the conductive medium to seep in and alter the measurement. To measure retinal resistivity without compression or rupture, we applied electrical resistance tomography using a planar multielectrode array with a 30 m pitch. Voltage waveforms generated in response to current injected from one electrode were measured on other electrodes in the array, at distances ranging from 30 to 600 m. Data from wild-type and degenerated rat retinas were analyzed using two methods: a commercial inversion software, Res2DInv, and a custom machine learning-based decoder, with healthy retina approximated as a 4-layer structure and degenerated retina - as a 3-layer one.
